kaviśekharetibirudavatā jyotirīśvareṇa viracitaḥ
pañcasāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Pañcasāyaka</s> (Five Arrows), composed by <s>Jyotirīśvara</s>, bearing the title <s>Kaviśekhara</s> (Crown of Poets).

children.text: prathamaḥ sāyakaḥ /

children.text: maṅgalācaraṇam /

children.text: ratiparimalasindhuḥ kāminīkelibandhur vihitabhuvanamodaḥ sevyamānapramodaḥ /
children.translated_text: An ocean of the fragrance of love, a companion in the amorous play of passionate women, the bestower of joy upon the world, delighting in pleasure,

children.text: jayati makaraketurmohanasyaikahetur viracitabahusevaḥ kāmibhiḥ kāmadevaḥ // JPanc_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Victorious is <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the God of Love), whose banner bears the <s>makara</s> (sea-creature), the sole cause of infatuation, served with manifold devotion by lovers.

children.text: granthakarturātmaparicayapradarśanam /

children.text: saṅgītāgamasatprameyaracanācāturyacintāmaṇiḥ prakhyātaḥ kaviśekharāṅkitapadaḥ śrījyotirīśaḥ kṛtī // JPanc_1.2 //
children.translated_text: A wish-fulfilling gem of skill in composing excellent works on music, <s>āgama</s> (sacred tradition), and valid subjects—the renowned <s>Śrī Jyotirīśa</s>, bearing the title <s>Kaviśekhara</s>, a man of accomplishment.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā manmathatantramīśvarakṛtaṃ vātsyāyanīyaṃ mataṃ goṇīputrakamūladevaracitaṃ bābhravyavākyāmṛtam /
children.translated_text: Having studied the <s>Manmathatantra</s> composed by <s>Īśvara</s>, the doctrine of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, the work composed by <s>Goṇīputra</s> and <s>Mūladeva</s>, the nectar of <s>Bābhravya</s>'s teachings,

children.text: śrīnandīśvararantidevabhaṇitaṃ kṣemendravidyāgamaṃ tenākalpyata pañcasāyaka iti prītipradaḥ kāminām // JPanc_1.3 //
children.translated_text: The works expounded by the illustrious <s>Nandīśvara</s> and <s>Ratideva</s>, and the learning of <s>Kṣemendra</s>—from all these was composed the <s>Pañcasāyaka</s>, which bestows delight upon lovers.

children.text: nāyakalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Characteristics of the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero).

children.text: sācāraḥ karuṇāmayaḥ kṛtamatirdātā 'vadātāśayaḥ kāmyaḥ kāmakalānidhiḥ suvacanaḥ strīṇāṃ mataḥ sundaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-mannered, compassionate, wise, generous, of pure disposition, desirable, a treasury of the arts of love, eloquent, esteemed by women, handsome,

children.text: āḍhyo nītipaṭuḥ kṣamī ca kutukī śūraḥ kulīno yuvā saṅkṣepādiha nāyako nigaditaḥ saṅgītaśikṣānvitaḥ // JPanc_1.4 //
children.translated_text: Wealthy, skilled in statecraft, patient, curious, valiant, of noble birth, youthful—in brief, the <s>nāyaka</s> is described here as one endowed with training in music.

children.text: pīṭhamardalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Characteristics of the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (confidant).

children.text: ācāre vinaye naye ca sukṛtau tauryatrike 'kṛtrimaḥ śāstre kautukaśilpanāṭakavidhau nānākalākauśale /
children.translated_text: Genuine in conduct, discipline, policy, and meritorious action; in the triad of performing arts, in the sciences, in the arts of amusement, drama, and various crafts and skills,

children.translated_text: Expert in knowing the sentiments and gestures [of others], clever in the arrangement of all wit and humor, reasoning and counter-reasoning; a knower of secrets, of steadfast friendship, and eloquent—such should the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> always be.

children.text: padminīlakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Characteristics of the <s>padminī</s> (lotus-woman).

children.translated_text: Fond of light diet, skilled in amorous sport, with a voice like a swan, proud, bashful, devoted to the worship of elders and gods—such a heroine is the <s>padminī</s>.

children.text: citriṇīlakṣaṇam /

children.text: śyāmā padmamukhī kuraṅganayanā kṣāmodarī vatsalā saṅgītāgamavedinī varatanustuṅgastanī śilpinī /

gurukucayugabhārā gauradehā natāṅgī taruṇahariṇanetrā kopanā vītalajjā /
vividhamadhuravākyā matsyamāṃsānuraktā munibhiriyamanarghā yakṣasattvā pradiṣṭā // JPanc_1.32 //
giriviharaṇavijñā rātrisañcāravīrā malinapiśunacittā kutsitāhāraceṣṭā /
vikṛtavadanacandrā kṛṣṇavarṇā 'tikharvā malinavasanaraktā kīrtitā pretasattvā // JPanc_1.33 //
iti kaviśekharaśrījyotirīśvarakaviracite pañcasāyake jātyādisamuddeśo nāma prathamaḥ sāyakaḥ /
atha dvitīyaḥ sāyakaḥ /
ratabhedāḥ /
āyāmaiḥ pariṇāhakaiśca puruṣāḥ liṅgairvarāṅgaiḥ striyo jñātavyāśca rasagṛhāruṇasamākhyātāṅgulaiḥ sarvataḥ /
jātyā te 'pi śaśā vṛṣāśca turagāḥ prājñaiḥ smṛtāstā punar mṛgyaścā kariṇīti vistarabhayātsaṅkṣipya niṣkṛṣyate // JPanc_2.1 //
śaśakahariṇapatnyorgoturaṅgyostathaiva hayagajapatināryorekarūpaṃ rataṃ syāt /
iha bhavati nitāntaṃ prītiranyonyayogād anumaraṇaśakyaṃ strī kathaṃ svīkaroti // JPanc_2.2 //
mṛgīvṛṣaṃ cedvṛṣabhīturaṅgamatyuccametaddvitayaṃ vadanti /
aśvāśaśaṃ gokariṇīsamutthaṃ nīcadvayaṃ tuṣṭikaraṃ na yūnoḥ // JPanc_2.3 //
mṛgīhayaṃ hastivadhūśaśaṃ cetatyuccanīcaṃ surataṃ vadanti /
pramāṇabhede 'pi na dravanti tasminna tṛpyanti nitambavatyaḥ // JPanc_2.4 //
proktaratānāmuttamamadhyamādhamatvam /
strīpuṃsayostulyarataṃ praśastaṃ madhyadvayaṃ madhyamamāmananti /
atyuccakaṃ cāpyatinīcakaṃ ca nindyaṃ ratajñaiḥ surataṃ pradiṣṭam // JPanc_2.5 //
prītiḥ samā syātsurate samākhye nīcadvaye yoṣita eva tuṣṭiḥ /
atyuccake vā 'pyatinīcake vā tuṣṭirna puṃsāṃ na ca sundarīṇām // JPanc_2.6 //
vegabhedātsuratabhedāḥ /
pracaṇḍavego 'pyatha madhyavegastathā 'paraḥ syāllaghunāmadheyaḥ /
puṃsastaruṇyā ubhayorapīha tridhā kavīndrāḥ surataṃ vadanti // JPanc_2.7 //
idānīṃ śaśādīnāṃ svarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
dīrghākṣāḥ sthūladehā laghusamadaśanā lambakarṇā suvāco grīvāyāṃ jānudeśe karakamalatale kālimānaṃ vahantaḥ /
alpāhārālpaśaucā dinamadhiśayinaḥ kāntimanto balāḍhyāḥ krīḍāvanto vinītā laghutarasuratāḥ puṇyabhājaḥ śaśāḥ syuḥ // JPanc_2.8 //
sucārukeśo mṛduvāk suveśaḥ sudīrghakaṇṭhaścapalaḥ sunetraḥ /
suraktapāṇiḥ samadantapaṅktiḥ saubhāgyayuktaḥ kathito mṛgo 'yam // JPanc_2.9 //
sphārākārāḥ sadarpāḥ suratarasakalālampaṭāḥ sundarāṅgā vyūḍhoraskāḥ surūpāḥ susamajaṭhariṇo māṃsalā lolanetrāḥ /
atyantaprauḍhavāco 'parilaghudhṛtayaḥ krodhanā madhyavegā ukṣāṇo liṅgamīṣadvitatanavamitairaṅgulīkairvahanti // JPanc_2.10 //
kārye dhṛṣṭā baliṣṭhāḥ sitaśamadaśanāḥ pīvarāsyā varākṣā grīvābāhūrudīrghāḥ parahitaniratāḥ sāttvikāḥ snigdhavācaḥ /
nirlajjāścāruśīlāḥ pṛthutaragatayaścaṇḍasambhogaraktā aśvā liṅgaṃ vahanto yuvatijanamataṃ bhānusaṅkhyāṅgulīkam // JPanc_2.11 //
mṛgyādīnāṃ svarūpanirūpaṇam /
mṛdvaṅgī dīrghanetrā varabisalatikākomalā dīrghabāhuḥ śoṇāmbhojābhirāmaṃ vahati karayugaṃ hrasvamadhyā sukeśī /
suśroṇīḥ kambukaṇṭhī pṛthukucayugalā yā vahatyaṅgulīkaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ kandarpagehaṃ kathayati hariṇīṃ tāmiha jyotirīśaḥ // JPanc_2.12 //
vyānimnottuṅgaśīrṣā bahutarakapiśasthūlakeśapracārā cañcannīlāmbujākṣī sulalitavadanā tuṅgavakṣojabhārā /
gambhīrāvartanābhirvalibhirupagatā śroṇibhārālasāṅgī seyaṃ randhrāṅgulīkaṃ vahati rataguhārandhrakaṃ vai turaṅgī // JPanc_2.13 //
sthūlāṅgī sthūlagaṇḍā laghutaranayanā sthūlanīlālpakeśā bimbauṣṭhī pīnabāhuḥ kaṭhinagurukucā hīnaparvā 'tiduṣṭā /
nirlajjā rāsabhoktistaralitavadanā sarvadā kaṣṭasādhyā nirdiṣṭā hastinīyaṃ vahati ravisamairaṅgulairguhyadeśam // JPanc_2.14 //
atha strīṇāmavasthāviśeṣāḥ kathyante /
ṣoḍaśavarṣavayaskāṃ bālāmityālapanti dhīmantaḥ /
viṃśāttaruṇīṃ triṃśātprauḍhāṃ pañcāśato vṛddhām // JPanc_2.15 //
bālā nūtanasaṅgame ratikarī sāndrāndhakāre bhaved āloke sukhamātanoti taruṇī sambhogalīlāvidhau /
āloke 'pi sukhāyate sarabhasaṃ prauḍhā tamisre 'ṅganā vṛddhā jīvitahāriṇī na kurute kutrāpi saukhyaṃ manāk // JPanc_2.16 //
atha deśaviśeṣāt strīsvarūpaṃ nirūpyate /
rūkṣāṅgī bahuvarṇinī calamatirgītapriyā cāṭulā śailāmbhonidhipārśvadeśavanitā prāyo bhavedīdṛśī /
ambhodāgamapuṣpamāsasamaye sevyā punaḥ prīṇitā gurvāhārasugandhimālyavasanasnigdhāṅgarāgādibhiḥ // JPanc_2.17 //
gūḍhagranthiraharniśaṃ hi sakale gātre vahapyacchatām ambhojaprasavāruṇottamakarā śītālayapreyasī /
saurāṣṭrī ca kaliṅgadeśayuvatiḥ kāmaṃ bhavetpittalā hemante śiśire narairavirataṃ sevyā yathākāṅkṣayā // JPanc_2.18 //
jñeyā kokilakākalīkalaravā medasvinī śītalā nidrāluśca śirīṣakomalatanuḥ snigdhānanā śleṣmalā /
vaṅgaśrīhaṭakāmarūpataruṇī śītādinā śaṅkitā gantavyā śaradi prakṛṣṭamadanā grīṣme narairādṛtā // JPanc_2.19 //
śucicaritavicitrā citrasambhogamitrā nakhadaśanaviraktā śilpaśikṣānuraktā /
sthiramatinijabandhuḥ kāmasarvasvasindhur bhavati ruciraveṣā kāminī madhyadeśā // JPanc_2.20 //
karakucakarajātāśleṣavinyāsadakṣā sakalasuratabandhurjñānavaidagdhyadakṣā /
nalaghunaguruvegā prāyaśaḥ kāmaraktā ramayati madhurālpaṃ sundarī tairabhuktī // JPanc_2.21 //
mṛduvacanavibhāgā komalānaṅgabhāgā vigataramaṇanī(bhī)tiḥ komalānaṅgagītiḥ /
dravati jhaṭiti kāntā citrasambhogadakṣā ramayati kila kaulī kīrtitā vaṅgīgauḍī // JPanc_2.22 //
karatalahatituṣṭā bāhyasambhogahṛṣṭā ciranidhuvanasādhyā mālavī dhūrtavākyā /
children.translated_text: Pleased by the striking of palms, delighted by external pleasures, achievable in love-making after a long time, the <s>Mālavī</s> (woman of Mālava) is deceitful in speech;

children.text: sukhayati sukhavegā vyañjitānaṅgarāgā capalapiśunaśīlā syādiyaṃ colabālā // JPanc_2.23 //
children.translated_text: she gives delight with a rush of pleasure, manifesting the flush of passion; fickle and treacherous by nature — such is this <s>Cola</s> maiden. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.23 //

children.text: kuvalayadalavarṇā cārutāṭaṅkakarṇā cakitahariṇanetrā phullarājīvavaktrā /
children.translated_text: Dark as a blue lotus petal, with beautiful earrings adorning her ears, with eyes like a startled deer, with a face like a full-blown lotus,

children.text: laghunidhuvanaraktā 'kaṣṭasambhogasaktā sulalitagatireṣā gurjarī cāruveṣā // JPanc_2.24 //
children.translated_text: quick to passion in love-making, averse to rough union, of graceful gait — this is the <s>Gurjarī</s> (woman of Gujarat), of charming attire. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.24 //

children.text: alasavalitadṛṣṭirdivyarūpāṅgayaṣṭiḥ kaṭhinamadanavegā duḥkhasādhyā prayoge /
children.translated_text: With languid, rolling glances and a divine, beautiful figure, of fierce force of passion, difficult to satisfy in the act of love,

children.text: viramati suratānte kopamāyāti kānte vividhapuruṣalolā saindhavī duṣṭaśīlā // JPanc_2.25 //
children.translated_text: she ceases at the end of love-making and shows anger toward her beloved; fond of various men, the <s>Saindhavī</s> (woman of Sindh) is of wicked disposition. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.25 //

children.text: pulakakarajadātrī duṣṭavākyābhidhātrī viṣamasuratapātrī niścitaṃ kālarātrī /
children.translated_text: Bestowing horripilation with her nails, speaking harsh words, a vessel of violent love-making, truly a night of death (<s>kālarātrī</s>) —

children.text: iti bhavati purandhrī kośalāvantikā strī kavalayati ratārtā śrūyate pūrvavārtā // JPanc_2.26 //
children.translated_text: thus is the married woman of <s>Kośala</s> and <s>Avantī</s>; she devours in the throes of passion — such is the tale heard of old. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.26 //

children.text: pikavaramṛduvācaḥ komalāṅgyaḥ suramyā vyapagatabhayalajjāḥ sāhasinyaḥ svatantrāḥ /
children.translated_text: With voices sweet as the finest cuckoo, of soft limbs, most lovely, free from fear and shame, bold, independent,

children.text: laghunidhuvanasādhyāścīnasauvīrabhedadraviḍamalayajātāḥ sundarāṅgyastaruṇyaḥ // JPanc_2.27 //
children.translated_text: quick to passion in love-making — the women born in <s>Cīna</s>, <s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>Draviḍa</s>, and <s>Malaya</s> are beautiful-limbed and youthful. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.27 //

children.text: sakalasuratadakṣā siddhisaubhāgyavaśyā daśanavasanapānaprītibhājaḥ salajjāḥ /
children.translated_text: Skilled in all arts of love, won over by success and good fortune, partaking of delight in biting, garments, and drink, yet modest,

children.text: karajalikhanadakṣāścaṇḍavegābhiramyāḥ kusumasurabhayaḥ syurmadratailaṅganāryaḥ // JPanc_2.28 //
children.translated_text: skilled in scratching with nails, delightful with fierce vigor, fragrant as flowers — such are the women of <s>Tailaṅga</s> (Telugu country). // <s>JPanc</s> 2.28 //

children.text: suratasavimardapremavatyaḥ pracaṇḍāḥ karajadaśanakeśāśleṣasañjñāvihīnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Passionate in the clash of love-making, fierce, bereft of the restraints of scratching, biting, hair-pulling, and embracing,

children.text: sahajamalinacittāḥ pauṇḍrakāmbojajātāḥ karatalalayatuṣṭāḥ kāmarūpāṅganāḥ syuḥ // JPanc_2.29 //
children.translated_text: naturally impure of mind, born of <s>Pauṇḍra</s> and <s>Kāmboja</s>, pleased by rhythmic clapping — such are the women of <s>Kāmarūpa</s>. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.29 //

children.text: gāḍhaṃ saṃśliṣya kaṇṭhe likhati kararuhaiḥ sarvataḥ kāntadehaṃ keśeṣvākṛṣya cumbatyadharamavirataṃ muṣṭighātaṃ dadāti /
children.translated_text: Clasping the neck tightly, she scratches her beloved's entire body with her nails on all sides, pulling his hair she kisses his lips unceasingly, and strikes with her fists;

children.text: tṛptiṃ no yāti śīghraṃ dravati na ca rate caṇḍavegā pragalbhā jñātavyā paṇḍitendrairatikalitaratirlāṭakarṇāṭanārī // JPanc_2.30 //
children.translated_text: she does not quickly reach satisfaction nor does she melt in passion — fierce and bold; the woman of <s>Lāṭa</s> and <s>Karṇāṭa</s>, of exceedingly intense passion, should be known by the wisest. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.30 //

children.text: duṣṭā durgandhadehāḥ paśusamasuratāścumbanaśleṣahīnāḥ serṣyā mlecchāṅganāḥ syurlaghurataniratāḥ pārvatīyāśca nāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wicked, with foul-smelling bodies, coupling like animals, devoid of kissing and embracing, jealous — such are the <s>Mleccha</s> (barbarian) women; devoted to quick love-making are also the mountain women;

children.text: kāśmīrābhīragandhyāḥ sakalarasakalāmodadakṣā nitāntaṃ sādhyā deśānusārādiha paṭumatibhiryoṣitaḥ sarvadaiva // JPanc_2.31 //
children.translated_text: the women of <s>Kāśmīra</s>, <s>Ābhīra</s>, and <s>Gandhāra</s> are supremely skilled in all the arts and flavors of love; women should always be won over by men of sharp intellect according to the customs of each region. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.31 //

children.text: jātestattvaṃ samastaṃ nikhilaśaśikalābodhanaṃ sattvavṛttiṃ mṛgyādīnāṃ vaśatvaṃ madanarasakalākautukaṃ cāpyaśeṣam /
children.translated_text: The complete truth of their birth, the understanding of all phases of the moon, the nature of temperament, the subjugation of deer-eyed women, and all the curiosities of the arts of love —

children.text: itthaṃ yaḥ kāminīnāṃ kalayati caritaṃ deśasātmyena samyag yāvajjīvaṃ sa tasyāḥ prabhavati hṛdaye prāṇanāthaḥ sukhāya // JPanc_2.32 //
children.translated_text: he who properly understands the conduct of women according to the customs of their region, he becomes the lord of her life and the source of delight for her heart, as long as he lives. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.32 //

children.text: yonibhedanirūpaṇam /
children.translated_text: Description of the types of <s>yoni</s> (female organ). /

children.text: sparśena paṅkajasamā taruṇījanānām abhyantare ca guṭikāsamadeśakā ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>yoni</s> of young women that is soft as a lotus to the touch, and with a bead-like protuberance inside,

children.text: yonirbhavedatha valiprakārāvakīrṇā gojihvikāsukharakarkaśagarbhadeśā // JPanc_2.33 //
children.translated_text: or the <s>yoni</s> covered with wrinkled folds, rough inside like a cow's tongue — // <s>JPanc</s> 2.33 //

children.text: atyuttamā prakathitā prathamā kavīndrair madhyā ca madhyamavidhā kila sampradiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The first is declared by the foremost poets to be most excellent, and the second is designated as middling;

children.text: śeṣadvayaṃ madanakelikalārasajñair nindyaṃ sadaiva kathitaṃ suratotsaveṣu // JPanc_2.34 //
children.translated_text: the remaining two are always said to be contemptible in the festivals of love by connoisseurs of the arts and flavors of love. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.34 //

children.text: vahnirna śāntimupayāti kadā 'pi kāṣṭhair nāmbhonidhirviramati pracuraiḥ payobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Fire is never quenched by [any amount of] firewood, nor does the ocean cease [to grow] with abundant waters,

children.text: nāpyantako jagati jantubhireti toṣaṃ vāmā 'pi naiva puruṣaiḥ khalu yāti tṛptim // JPanc_2.35 //
children.translated_text: nor is Death ever satisfied by the creatures of the world; so too a woman is never truly satiated by men. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.35 //

children.text: tasmānnareṇa ratiraṅgavicakṣaṇena māyāmupāsya sakalāṃ svaśarīrasādhyām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by a man skilled in the theater of love, having mastered all the wiles achievable through his own body,

children.text: tāsāṃ manoharaṇameva paraṃ vidheyaṃ no veda ko 'pi hṛdayaṃ khalu kāminīnām // JPanc_2.36 //
children.translated_text: the supreme task should be the captivation of their hearts — for no one truly knows the heart of women. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.36 //

children.text: prītibhedanirūpaṇam /
children.translated_text: Description of the types of affection (<s>prīti</s>). /

children.text: srakcandanāmbaramanoharabhakṣyabhojyair nānāvidhairupacitā viṣayaiḥ sadaiva /
children.translated_text: That [affection] which is always nourished by garlands, sandalwood, garments, delightful foods and meals, and various sensory objects —

children.text: prītiḥ smṛtā viṣayajeti kavipravīraiḥ sādṛśyayogasubhagā kathitā sadaiva // JPanc_2.37 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>viṣayajā prīti</s> (sensory love) by eminent poets; it is always said to be blessed through the conjunction of similarity. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.37 //

children.text: ākheṭaśilpasurapūjanakeliraṅgasaṅgītasevanavidhāvupacīyate yā /
children.translated_text: That [affection] which is fostered through hunting, arts, worship of the gods, sports, theater, attendance at concerts, and similar activities —

children.text: abhyāsakauśalavaśena kṛśodarīṇām ābhyāsakī nigaditā kavibhiḥ purāṇaiḥ // JPanc_2.38 //
children.translated_text: that, arising from the power of habitual practice, is called <s>ābhyāsakī</s> (love through practice) by ancient poets, with regard to slender-waisted women. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.38 //

children.text: strīṇāṃ rāgavināśahetavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Causes of the destruction of women's passion. /

children.text: dāridraduḥkhabhayaviklavamānarogair udvegakopatanutādibhirīśvarāṇām /
children.translated_text: Due to poverty, sorrow, fear, distress, pride, illness, agitation, anger, emaciation, and such [afflictions] of their lords —

children.text: rāgaṃ tyajanti vanitā iha vistarasya bhītyā na cāsya kathitaḥ sakalo vivartaḥ // JPanc_2.39 //
children.translated_text: women abandon their passion in this world; and the complete account of this has not been told, for fear of prolixity. // <s>JPanc</s> 2.39 //

children.text: iti śrīkaviśekharajyotīśvaraviracite pañcasāyake dvitīyaḥ sāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second arrow (<s>sāyaka</s>) in the <s>Pañcasāyaka</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Jyotirīśvara Kaviśekhara</s>. /

children.text: atha tṛtīyaḥ sāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now the third arrow (<s>sāyaka</s>). /

children.text: dehadaurgandhyaharaṇayogāḥ /
children.translated_text: Recipes for removing body odor. /

children.text: prāgaṅgarāgaḥ puruṣeṇa kāryaḥ sriyā ca sambhogasukhāya gātre /
children.translated_text: A man should first apply body unguent (<s>aṅgarāga</s>) on his body, and a woman likewise, for the sake of the pleasure of union;

children.text: tasmādahaṃ gandhavidhānamādau vilāsinaḥ sarvamudīrayāmi // JPanc_3.1 //
children.translated_text: therefore, I shall first expound all the preparations of fragrance for the pleasure-seeker. // <s>JPanc</s> 3.1 //

children.text: harītakīlodhramariṣṭapatraṃ saptacchado dāḍimakalkalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>lodhra</s> (Symplocos racemosa), <s>ariṣṭa</s> (soapberry) leaves, <s>saptacchada</s> (Alstonia scholaris), and pomegranate paste —

children.text: eṣo 'ṅganāyāḥ kathitaḥ kavīndraiḥ śarīradaurgandhyaharaḥ pralepaḥ // JPanc_3.2 //
children.translated_text: this paste, described by foremost poets, removes the body odor of a woman. // <s>JPanc</s> 3.2 //

children.text: harītakīcandanamustanāgairuśīralodhrāmayarātritulyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With <s>harītakī</s>, sandalwood, <s>musta</s> (nutgrass), <s>nāga</s> (Mesua ferrea), <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver), <s>lodhra</s>, <s>amaya</s>, and <s>rātri</s> (turmeric) in equal parts —

children.text: strīpuṃsayorgharmajagātragandhaṃ vināśayatyāśu vilepanaṃ ca // JPanc_3.3 //
children.translated_text: this unguent quickly destroys the sweat-born body odor of both men and women. // <s>JPanc</s> 3.3 //

children.text: harītaīśrīphalamustayuktairbimbīphalaiḥ pūtakarañjabījaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With <s>harītakī</s>, <s>śrīphala</s> (wood-apple), <s>musta</s> (nutgrass), <s>bimbī</s> fruit, and <s>pūtakarañja</s> (Caesalpinia bonduc) seeds —

children.text: kakṣādidaurgandhyamatiprabhūtaṃ vināśayatyāśu haṭhena yogaḥ // JPanc_3.4 //
children.translated_text: this recipe quickly and forcefully destroys even very excessive armpit and other body odor. // <s>JPanc</s> 3.4 //

children.text: (sacandanośīrakabilvapatraiḥ kolākṣamajjāgurunāgapuṣpaiḥ /

children.translated_text: When the abode of love is smeared, it flows quickly through this medicinal preparation—thus declares the king <s>Rantideva</s>, lord of poets.

children.text: liṅgasthūlīkaraṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Section on enlargement of the <s>liṅga</s> (male organ).

children.text: sakuṣṭhamātaṅgabalābalānāṃ vacāśvagandhāgajapippalīnām /
children.translated_text: Of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>mātaṅgabalā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>aśvagandhā</s>, and <s>gajapippalī</s> (elephant pepper),

children.text: turaṅgaśatrornavanītayogāllepena liṅgaṃ muśalatvameti // JPanc_3.43 //
children.translated_text: With a paste application of fresh butter of the enemy of the horse [i.e., buffalo], the member becomes pestle-like.

children.text: sarodhrakāśīśaturaṅgagandhāmātaṅgagandhāparipācitena /
children.translated_text: With oil prepared from <s>sarodhra</s>, <s>kāśīśa</s> (green vitriol), <s>turaṅgagandhā</s>, and <s>mātaṅgagandhā</s>,

children.text: tailena vṛddhiṃ khalu yānti śīghraṃ varāṅgakarṇastanamehanāni // JPanc_3.44 //
children.translated_text: The intimate organ, ears, breasts, and member quickly increase in size, indeed.

children.text: atha dhvajadṛḍhīkaraṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on hardening of the member.

children.text: hayāripatraṃ navanītapiṣṭaṃ vacābalānāgabalāmayaiśca /
children.translated_text: The leaf of the enemy of the horse [buffalo], ground with fresh butter, with <s>vacā</s>, <s>balā</s>, and <s>nāgabalā</s>,

children.text: lepena liṅgaṃ sahasaiva puṃsāṃ lohopamaṃ syāditi dṛṣṭametat // JPanc_3.45 //
children.translated_text: With a paste application, the member of men suddenly becomes iron-like—this has been observed.

children.text: atha vīryastambhanasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on <s>vīryastambhana</s> (semen retention).

children.text: kṣīreṇa bastasya ca baddhamūlaṃ lajjālumūlaṃ svayameva piṣṭvā /
children.translated_text: Having ground the root of <s>baddhamūla</s> and <s>lajjālu</s> (sensitive plant) with the milk of a goat,

children.text: yastu svapādau parilipya śete reto na tasya sravate kadācit // JPanc_3.46 //
children.translated_text: He who smears his own feet and sleeps—his semen never flows.

children.text: śveteṣupuṅkhākhyataroḥ phalāni kṣīreṇa piṣṭvā vaṭapādapasya /
children.translated_text: Having ground the fruits of the tree called <s>śveteṣupuṅkha</s> (white arrow-feather) with the milk of a banyan tree,

children.text: karañjabījodaramadhyagāni badhnanti vīryaṃ vadane dhṛtāni // JPanc_3.47 //
children.translated_text: Placed inside the kernel of <s>karañja</s> seeds, when held in the mouth, they arrest the semen.

children.text: śveteṣupuṅkhācaraṇaṃ gṛhītvā puṣyārkayoge puruṣasya kaṭyām /
children.translated_text: Having taken the root of <s>śveteṣupuṅkha</s>, [bound] on the waist of a man during the conjunction of <s>Puṣya</s> [asterism] and Sunday,

children.text: kumārikākartitasūtrakeṇa baddhaṃ na yātyāśu manojajīram // JPanc_3.48 //
children.translated_text: With a thread cut by a maiden, when bound, the fluid of the love-god does not quickly depart.

children.text: ādāya kṛṣṇetarakākajaṅghāmūlaṃ sitāmbhoruhakeśaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having taken the root of <s>kṛṣṇetara-kākajaṅghā</s> (non-black crow-shin plant) and the stamens of a white lotus,

children.text: kṣaudrena piṣṭvā pariliptanābheḥ stambhaṃ prayātyāśu narasya bījam // JPanc_3.49 //
children.translated_text: Having ground them with honey and smeared the navel, the seed of a man quickly becomes arrested.

children.text: atha vaśīkaraṇatilakasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s> (subjugation) <s>tilaka</s> (forehead-mark).

children.text: mañjiṣṭhatoyadavacāsitabhānumūlaiḥ svīyāṅgaśoṇitayutaiḥ samakuṣṭhakaiśca /
children.translated_text: With <s>mañjiṣṭha</s> (madder), <s>toyada</s> (nutgrass), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), white <s>bhānumūla</s> (sun-plant root), combined with one's own blood, and <s>kuṣṭhaka</s> in equal parts,

children.text: kṛtvā lalāṭaphalake tilakaṃ kṛtajño lokatrayaṃ vaśayati kṣaṇamātrakeṇa // JPanc_3.50 //
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>tilaka</s> (forehead-mark) on the forehead, the grateful one subjugates the three worlds in a mere instant.

children.text: atha vaśīkaraṇāñjanasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s> (subjugation) collyrium.

children.text: devīmahotsavadine kila kajjalaṃ yat siddhārthakasya surasena narottamāṅge /
children.translated_text: On the day of the great festival of the Goddess, the collyrium that is prepared from mustard seeds by a noble man upon the head of a corpse

children.text: niṣpātitaṃ naravareṇa niśi śmaśāne tannetragaṃ bhuvanameva vaśaṃ karoti // JPanc_3.51 //
children.translated_text: At night in the cremation ground—when placed in the eyes, it subjugates the entire world.

children.text: atha vaśīkaraṇacūrṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s> (subjugation) powder.

children.text: kuṣṭhotpalaṃ madhukarasya ca patrayugmaṃ mūlaṃ tathā tagarajaṃ sitakākajaṅghā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṣṭha</s>, <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), and a pair of leaves of the bee [possibly basil], the root of <s>tagara</s> (valerian), and white <s>kākajaṅghā</s>,

children.text: yasyāḥ śirogatamidaṃ vihitaṃ tu cūrṇaṃ dāsībhavejjhaṭiti sā taruṇī na citram // JPanc_3.52 //
children.translated_text: When this powder is placed upon the head of whichever [woman], she instantly becomes a slave-girl—there is no wonder in this.

children.text: atha vaśīkaraṇalepanasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on <s>vaśīkaraṇa</s> (subjugation) ointment.

children.text: savyena pāṇikamalena ratāvasāne yo retasā nijabhavena vilāsadakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, skilled in amorous sport, at the end of lovemaking, with his own semen using his left lotus-hand,

children.text: vāmaṃ vilimpati padaṃ sahasaiva yasyās tasyaiva sā bhavati nātra vikalpabhāvaḥ // JPanc_3.53 //
children.translated_text: Smears the left foot of whichever [woman]—she instantly becomes his alone; there is no room for doubt here.

children.text: sambhogaśeṣasamaye nijakāntameḍhraṃ yā kāminī spṛśati vāmapadāmbujena /
children.translated_text: The woman who at the end of intercourse touches the member of her own beloved with her left lotus-foot,

children.text: tasyāḥ patiḥ sapadi vindati dāsabhāvaṃ goṇīsutena kathitaḥ kila yāgarājaḥ // JPanc_3.54 //
children.translated_text: Her husband instantly attains the state of a servant—this king of rituals was told by the son of <s>Goṇī</s>.

children.text: sindhūtthamākṣikakapotamalāni piṣṭvā liṅgaṃ vilipya taruṇīṃ ramate naro yaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ground sea-born [salt], honey, and pigeon droppings, he who smears his member and makes love to a young woman,

children.text: sā 'nyaṃ prayāti puruṣaṃ na kadā 'pi kāmaṃ dāsībhavedatimanoharadivyamūrtiḥ // JPanc_3.55 //
children.translated_text: She never goes to another man with desire—she becomes a slave-girl, though of exceedingly beautiful divine form.

children.text: bhallūkameḍhraghanasāramadhūni piṣṭvā liptadhvajo nidhuvanaṃ vidadhīta yasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ground the penis of a bear, camphor, and honey, he who performs lovemaking with his member smeared, to whichever [woman],

children.text: sā ' 'hlādinī kusumasāyakasannatāṅgī vaśyā bhaveccirataraṃ na hi saṃśayo 'tra // JPanc_3.56 //
children.translated_text: She, delightful and with body bent by the flower-arrowed [love-god], becomes subjugated for a very long time—there is no doubt here.

children.text: gorocanāśiśiradīdhitiśambhubījakāśmīracandanayutaiḥ kanakadraveṇa /
children.translated_text: With gold liquid mixed with <s>gorocanā</s> (ox-bezoar), cool-rayed [camphor], <s>Śambhu</s>-seed [dhattūra], saffron, and sandalwood,

children.text: liptadhvajaḥ pariramatyabalāṃ naro yas tasyāḥ sa eva hṛdaye mukuṭatvameti // JPanc_3.57 //
children.translated_text: the man whose flag [i.e., body] is anointed thus sports with the woman — he alone becomes the crown upon her heart. // JPanc_3.57 //

children.text: atha vaśīkaraṇadhūpasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on incense for subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>).

children.text: śṛṅgīvacāyuvatisarjarasaṃ samānaṃ kṛtvā truṭiṃ malayajaṃ ca ṣaḍeva miśram /
children.translated_text: Having made equal [parts of] <s>śṛṅgī</s> (a plant), <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>yuvatisarjaresa</s> (resin of young <s>sarja</s> tree), <s>truṭi</s> (small cardamom), and sandalwood — six [ingredients] mixed together,

children.text: yo dhūpayennijagṛhaṃ vasanaṃ śarīraṃ tasyāpi dāsa iva mohamupaiti lokaḥ // JPanc_3.58 //
children.translated_text: whoever fumigates his own house, garments, and body [with this] — even the world becomes enslaved to him like a servant. // JPanc_3.58 //

children.text: atha vaśīkaraṇamantrasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on mantras for subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>).

children.text: madamadapadamādau mādayeti dvivāraṃ tadanu ca likhanīyaṃ saukhyadaṃ hrīṃ ca tasmāt /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>mada</s>' first, then '<s>mādaya</s>' twice, then after that one should write '<s>hrīṃ</s>' which bestows pleasure;

children.text: atha ca padamupānte nāmarūpādisañjño bhavati madanamantraḥ svāhayā saṃyuto 'yam // JPanc_3.59 //
children.translated_text: then at the end, the word denoting the name and form [of the desired person] — this becomes the <s>Madana</s> (love) mantra, concluded with <s>svāhā</s>. // JPanc_3.59 //

children.text: 'oṃ mada mada mādaya mādaya hrīṃ amukīṃ vaśamānaya svāhā'
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ mada mada mādaya mādaya hrīṃ</s> [name of the woman] <s>vaśamānaya svāhā</s>.'

children.text: śataśataparijāpāt syādayaṃ siddhidātā daśadaśakusumānāṃ lohitānāṃ ca homāt /
children.translated_text: By reciting this a hundred-hundred [ten thousand] times, it becomes the bestower of success; and by the oblation of ten-ten [a hundred] red flowers.

children.text: iha tu sakalakāryaṃ vāmahastena kāryam upadiśati samāsājjyotirīśaḥ svarūpam // JPanc_3.60 //
children.translated_text: Here, everything should be done with the left hand — <s>Jyotirīśa</s> (the author) teaches [this] method in brief. // JPanc_3.60 //

children.text: asya mantrasya daśasahastrasaṅkhyākonmito japaḥ, raktavarṇaiḥ prasūnairmadhunā ghṛtena ca homaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / sarvaṃ vāmahastena kartavyam / atha dhyānam
children.translated_text: The recitation (<s>japa</s>) of this mantra is measured at ten thousand times; the oblation should be performed with red-colored flowers, honey, and ghee. Everything for the left-hand [practice].

children.text: kanakaruciramūrtiḥ kuṇḍalākṛṣṭacāpo yuvatihṛdayamadhye niścalāropitākṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: With a form radiant as gold, bow drawn by the ear-ring [of <s>Kāma</s>], his gaze firmly fixed upon the heart of the young woman,

children.text: iti manasi manojaṃ dhyāyayedyo japastho vaśayati sa samastaṃ bhūtalaṃ mantraśaktyā // JPanc_3.61 //
children.translated_text: one who meditates in the mind upon <s>Manoja</s> (<s>Kāma</s>, the love god) thus, while seated in <s>japa</s>, subjugates the entire world through the power of the mantra. // JPanc_3.61 //

children.text: atha cāmuṇḍamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> mantra.

children.text: cāmuṇḍe prathamaṃ jayeti kathitaṃ sambodhanaṃ mohaya jñātavyaṃ vaśamānayeti ca padaṃ sādhyaṃ dvitīyāyutam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Cāmuṇḍe</s>' first, then '<s>jaya</s>' is spoken as the address, '<s>mohaya</s>' — then the word '<s>vaśamānaya</s>' should be known along with the object [person's name] in the accusative;

children.text: svāhāntaḥ praṇavādireṣa prathitastantre mahāmohanaḥ sanmantraḥ kaviśekhareṇa kathito nāsmāddvitīyo bhuvi // JPanc_3.62 //
children.translated_text: ending with <s>svāhā</s>, beginning with <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) — this is the celebrated great-enchantment mantra in <s>Tantra</s>; the excellent mantra spoken by <s>Kaviśekhara</s> — there is no second [equal to it] on earth. // JPanc_3.62 //

children.text: 'oṃ cāmuṇḍe jaya cāmuṇḍe mohaya amukīṃ vaśamānaya svāhā' iti mantraḥ / asya mantrasya japa ekalakṣamitaḥ, palāśakusumairhomaḥ daśāṃśaṃ, sarvaṃ vāmahastena kartavyam / atha cāmuṇḍāyā dhyānam-
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ cāmuṇḍe jaya cāmuṇḍe mohaya</s> [name of the woman] <s>vaśamānaya svāhā</s>' — this is the mantra. The recitation of this mantra is measured at one hundred thousand times; with <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) flowers [for oblation].

children.text: daṃṣṭrākoṭivisaṅkaṭā suvadanā sāndrāndhakāre sthitā khaṭvāṅgāsinigūḍhadakṣiṇakarā vāme sapāśaṃ śiraḥ /
children.translated_text: With terrible fangs, beautiful-faced, standing in dense darkness, a skull-staff and sword concealed in the right hand, in the left a noose and a [severed] head,

children.text: śyāmā piṅgalamūrdhajā bhayakarī śārdūlacarmāmbarā cāmuṇḍā śavavāhinī japavidhau dhyeyā sadā sādhakaiḥ // JPanc_3.63 //
children.translated_text: dark-complexioned, tawny-haired, fearsome, wearing a tiger-skin garment — <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, riding a corpse, should always be meditated upon by practitioners during the recitation rite. // JPanc_3.63 //

children.text: atha viśveśvarīmantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Viśveśvarī</s> mantra.

children.text: oṅkāraḥ prathamaṃ namo nama iti proktaṃ ca tasmātpadaṃ cāmuṇḍe parikīrtitaṃ hili hili jñeyā ca sañjñā tataḥ /
children.translated_text: First '<s>Oṅkāra</s>' (<s>Oṃ</s>), then '<s>namo namaḥ</s>' is spoken, and after that the word '<s>cāmuṇḍe</s>' is proclaimed, then '<s>hili hili</s>' should be known as the sacred syllable;

children.text: jñātavyaṃ tu samānayeti ca padaṃ sanmantriṇāṃ sammato mantro 'yaṃ kaviśekhareṇa kathitaḥ khyātaḥ sadā siddhidaḥ // JPanc_3.64 //
children.translated_text: then the word '<s>samānaya</s>' (bring under control) should be known — this mantra is approved by true adepts; spoken by <s>Kaviśekhara</s>, it is celebrated and always bestows success. // JPanc_3.64 //

children.text:
'oṃ namo namaścāmuṇḍe hilī hili amukīṃ vaśamānaya svāhā'
asya mantrasya japa ekalakṣaparimitaḥ, taddaśāṃśaḥ palāśakusumairhomaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, sarvaṃ vāmahastena kartavyam //
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ namo namaścāmuṇḍe hilī hili</s> [name of the woman] <s>vaśamānaya svāhā</s>.' The recitation of this mantra is limited to one hundred thousand times; one-tenth of that [number] with <s>palāśa</s> flowers [for oblation].

children.text: athaviśveśvarīdhyānam /
children.translated_text: Now, the meditation on <s>Viśveśvarī</s>.

children.text: vajrāsaktaśarāsanā trinayanā savyetareṇāṅkuśaṃ vāmenāpi kareṇa pāśamurasi nyastottamāṅgasrajā /
children.translated_text: Seated on a vajra [thunderbolt seat], bow in hand, three-eyed, with a goad in the right hand and a noose in the left, wearing a garland of the best [skulls] placed on the chest,

children.text: vyāmuktorukacā karālavadanā vahniprabhā madhyagā dhyeyā jāpavidhau narairiti sadā viśveśvarī siddhaye // JPanc_3.65 //
children.translated_text: with flowing abundant hair, terrifying face, luminous as fire, stationed in the center — <s>Viśveśvarī</s> should always be meditated upon by men during the recitation rite for success. // JPanc_3.65 //

children.text: atha padminīvaśīkaraṇamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the mantra for subjugating the <s>padminī</s> [type of woman].

children.text: 'oṃ kāmeśvara ! mohaya svāhā' iti mantraḥ / anena mantreṇa madhumiśritajātikusumasahitaṃ tāmbūlamādityadine sahasravāramabhimantritaṃ padminyai dātavyam / padminī vaśyā bhavati //
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Kāmeśvara! mohaya svāhā</s>' — this is the mantra. With this mantra, a betel preparation mixed with honey and <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers should [be given] on a Sunday, a thousand times [recited].

children.text: atha citriṇīvaśīkaraṇamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the mantra for subjugating the <s>citriṇī</s> [type of woman].

children.text: 'oṃ paca paca oṃ vihaṅgama vihaṅgama oṃ kāmadevāya svāhā' iti mantraḥ / anena mantreṇa rambhāmūlajalabhāvitajātīphalamilitatāmbūlamādityadine pañcaśatavāramabhimantritaṃ citriṇyai dātavyam / citriṇī vaśyā bhavati //
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ paca paca oṃ vihaṅgama vihaṅgama oṃ Kāmadevāya svāhā</s>' — this is the mantra. With this mantra, a <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) fruit infused with the juice of plantain root [should be used].

children.text: atha śaṅkhinīvaśīkaraṇamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the mantra for subjugating the <s>śaṅkhinī</s> [type of woman].

children.text: 'oṃ hara hara oṃ paca paca kāmadevāya svāhā' iti mantraḥ / anena mantreṇa taragamūlaṃ śrīphalañcādityavāre aṣṭottaraśatavāramabhimantritaṃ śaṅkhinyai dātavyam / sā vaśyā bhavati //
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ hara hara oṃ paca paca Kāmadevāya svāhā</s>' — this is the mantra. With this mantra, <s>taraga</s> root and <s>śrīphala</s> (wood-apple) [should be used] on a Sunday, one hundred and eight times [recited].

children.text: atha hastinīvaśīkaraṇamantraḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the mantra for subjugating the <s>hastinī</s> [type of woman].

children.text: 'oṃ ciri ciri vaśaṃ kuru kāmadevāya svāhā' iti mantraḥ / anena mantreṇa ādityadine kṣaudrāktau kapotabhramarapakṣau tāmbūladale vinyasya aṣṭottaraśatamabhimantritaṃ kṛtvā hastinyai deyam / hastinī vaśyā bhavati //
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ ciri ciri vaśaṃ kuru Kāmadevāya svāhā</s>' — this is the mantra. With this mantra, on a Sunday, pigeon and bee wings anointed with honey [should be placed in] betel.

children.text: atha anicchāharaṇopāyanirūpaṇam /
children.translated_text: Now, the description of remedies for removing unwillingness (<s>anicchā</s>).

children.text: kṣīrodanaṃ dvijavarāya purā pradadyāt puṣyoddhṛtaṃ sitabalācaraṇaṃ kumāryā /
children.translated_text: One should first give rice cooked in milk to an excellent <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; then the feet of a maiden, gathered on <s>Puṣya</s> [lunar mansion], ground with white <s>balā</s> [plant],

children.text: piṣṭaṃ pradattamiti vairakṛtāmanicchāṃ niḥsārayediha muhurviditaprabhāvaḥ // JPanc_3.66 //
children.translated_text: when given [to the unwilling woman] — one who knows its power removes the unwillingness caused by enmity again and again. // JPanc_3.66 //

children.text: atha stanotthāpanasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on breast-firming.

children.text: mātaṅgakṛṣṇāmayavājigandhā vacāyutāḥ paryuṣitāmbumiśrāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mātaṅga</s> (elephant) [tusk powder], black <s>āmaya</s> (dried ginger), horse-musk, and <s>vacā</s> (sweet flag), mixed together with stale water,

children.text: hayāripatrīnavanītayogāt kurvanti pīnaṃ kucakumbhayugmam // JPanc_3.67 //
children.translated_text: combined with <s>hayāripatrī</s> (a plant) and fresh butter — they make the pair of breast-pots firm and full. // JPanc_3.67 //

children.text: vasā bhujaṅgasya hayāripatraṃ kolasya medaḥ samabhāgayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: The fat of a serpent, <s>hayāripatrī</s> (a plant) leaves, and the marrow of a <s>kola</s> (jujube) — combined in equal parts,

children.text: vakṣojakumbhaṃ madirāyatākṣyāḥ kurvanti pīnaṃ sakalaṃ haṭhena // JPanc_3.68 //
children.translated_text: they make the breast-pots of the woman with wine-long eyes firm and full entirely, by force. // JPanc_3.68 //

children.text: tailaṃ haṭhāddāḍimakalkasiddhaṃ siddhārthajaṃ lepanato nitāntam /
children.translated_text: Oil forcefully prepared with pomegranate paste, and mustard [oil] — by application, exceedingly,

children.text: nārīstanau cārutarau supīnau kuryādasau yogavaraḥ sadaiva // JPanc_3.69 //
children.translated_text: that excellent preparation always makes a woman's breasts beautiful and very full. // JPanc_3.69 //

children.text: śrīparṇikāyā rasakalkasiddhaṃ tilodbhavaṃ tailavaraṃ pradiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Oil of sesame, prepared with the juice-paste of <s>śrīparṇikā</s> (Gmelina arborea), is prescribed as the best;

children.text: plotena vakṣojayuge pradeyaṃ prayāti vṛddhiṃ patito 'pi nāryāḥ // JPanc_3.70 //
children.translated_text: applied to the pair of breasts with a cloth — even a woman's fallen [breasts] regain fullness. // JPanc_3.70 //

children.text: yonisaṃskārasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The section on preparation of the female organ (<s>yoni</s>).

children.text: prakṣālayennimbakaṣāyanīrairniśājyakṛṣṇāguruguggulūnām /
children.translated_text: One should wash with a decoction of <s>nimba</s> (neem); having fumigated the <s>yoni</s> at night with the smoke of <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), ghee, black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium),

children.text: dhūpena yoniṃ niśi dhūpayitvā nārī pramodaṃ vidadhāti bhartuḥ // JPanc_3.71 //
children.translated_text: the woman bestows delight upon her husband. // JPanc_3.71 //

children.text: jātīprasūnaiḥ sitasarṣapasya tailaṃ pacellaghvanale prakāmam /
children.translated_text: One should cook oil of white mustard with <s>jātī</s> (jasmine) flowers over a gentle fire thoroughly;

children.text: abhyaṅgayogena sadaiva yonau saubhāgyamāpnoti rate purandhrī // JPanc_3.72 //
children.translated_text: by the regular application of this ointment to the <s>yoni</s>, the woman attains good fortune in love-making. // JPanc_3.72 //

children.text: atha romaśātanasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on hair removal.

children.text: bhujaṅgacūrṇaṃ kaṭutailamadhye saptāhamādityakare nidheyam /
children.translated_text: Serpent powder should be placed in pungent oil for seven days in the rays of the sun;

children.text: tattailayogena vilāsinīnāṃ naśyanti romāṇi samūlameva // JPanc_3.73 //
children.translated_text: by the application of that oil, the body-hairs of beautiful women are destroyed, root and all. // JPanc_3.73 //

children.text: palāśabhasmānvitatālacūrṇaiḥ rambhāmbumiśrairupalipya bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having smeared again with <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) ash mixed with ground <s>tāla</s> (palmyra) powder and plantain water,

children.text: kandarpagehe mṛgalocanānāṃ romāṇi rohanti kadāpi naiva // JPanc_3.74 //
children.translated_text: the hairs in <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Kāma's) abode of the doe-eyed women never grow again. // JPanc_3.74 //

children.text: rambhājale saptadinaṃ vibhāvya bhasmeha kambormasṛṇaṃ ca paścāt /
children.translated_text: Having soaked in plantain water for seven days, then [mixing] ashes with fine <s>kambora</s> (camphor),

children.text: tālena yuktaṃ ca vilepanena romāṇi nirmūlayati kṣaṇena // JPanc_3.75 //
children.translated_text: combined with <s>tāla</s> (palmyra) [powder] — this depilatory removes hairs root and all in an instant. // JPanc_3.75 //

children.text: atha puṣpajananasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on inducing menstruation.

children.text: jyotiṣmatīkomalapatramagnau bhṛṣṭaṃ japāyāḥ kusumena piṣṭam /
children.translated_text: The tender leaves of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (Celastrus paniculatus), roasted in fire, ground with the flower of <s>japā</s> (hibiscus),

children.text: gṛhāmbunā pītamidaṃ yuvatyā karoti puṣpaṃ smaramandirasya // JPanc_3.76 //
children.translated_text: when drunk by a young woman with household water — it produces the flower [menstruation] in the abode of <s>Smara</s> (Kāma). // JPanc_3.76 //

children.text: atha garbhasādhāraṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the general section on conception.

children.text: turaṅgagandhāśrutavārisiddhamājaṃ payaḥ snānadine nipīya /
children.translated_text: Having drunk goat's milk prepared with horse-musk and <s>aśruta</s> water on a bathing day,

children.text: prāpnoti garbhaṃ niyamaṃ carantī vandhyā 'pi nūnaṃ puruṣaprasaṅgāt // JPanc_3.77 //
children.translated_text: even a barren woman, while observing the [prescribed] restraints, certainly conceives from union with a man. // JPanc_3.77 //

children.text: puṣyoddhṛtaṃ lākṣmaṇameva mūlaṃ bhartrā nipiṣṭaṃ saghṛtaṃ ca pītam /
children.translated_text: The very root of <s>lākṣmaṇa</s> (a plant), extracted on <s>Puṣya</s> [lunar mansion], ground by the husband with ghee and drunk,

children.text: kṣīraudanaṃ prāśya patiprasaṅgādgarbhaṃ vidhatte taruṇī na citram // JPanc_3.78 //
children.translated_text: having eaten rice-cooked-in-milk — from union with the husband, the young woman conceives; this is no wonder. // JPanc_3.78 //

children.text: yā bījapūradrumamūlamekaṃ kṣīreṇa siddhaṃ haviṣā vimiśram /
children.translated_text: She who drinks the single root of a <s>bījapūra</s> (citron) tree, cooked in milk and mixed with ghee,

children.text: ṛtau nipīya svapatiṃ prayāti dīrghāyuṣaṃ sā tanayaṃ prasūte // JPanc_3.79 //
children.translated_text: during her fertile period, and goes to her husband — she gives birth to a long-lived son. // JPanc_3.79 //

children.text: atha garbhasaṃsthāpanasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on stabilizing the fetus.

children.text: kaśeruśṛṅgāṭakajīvanākhyapayodharairaṇḍaśatāvarībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With <s>kaśeru</s> (a tuber), <s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water caltrop), <s>jīvana</s> (a plant), <s>payodharā</s> (a plant), <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), and <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus racemosus),

children.text: siddhaṃ payaḥ śarkarayā vimiśraṃ saṃsthāpayedgarbhamudīrṇaśūlam // JPanc_3.80 //
children.translated_text: milk prepared [with these] and mixed with sugar stabilizes the fetus [even when there is] acute pain. // JPanc_3.80 //

children.text: atha sukhaprasavasamuddeśaḥ / atha sukhaprasavamantraḥ -
children.translated_text: Now, the section on easy childbirth. Now, the mantra for easy childbirth:

children.text: oṃ ihāmṛtañca somaśca citrabhānuśca bhāmini /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> — may <s>Amṛta</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Citrabhānu</s> (the Sun), O beautiful woman,

children.text: uccaiḥśravā turaṅgāṇāṃ mandire nivasantu te // JPanc_3.81 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> (the celestial horse) among steeds — dwell in your womb! // JPanc_3.81 //

children.text: oṃ idamamamṛtamapāṃ samuddhṛtaṃ vai tava laghu garbhamimaṃ vimuñcatu stri /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> — this nectar, drawn up from the waters indeed, may it release your fetus quickly, O woman!

children.text: tadanalapavanārkavāsarāste saha lavaṇāmbudharairdiśantu śāntim // JPanc_3.82 //
children.translated_text: May fire, wind, and the sun, along with the salt-bearing clouds, grant you peace on that day! // JPanc_3.82 //

children.text: oṃ muktāḥ pāśā vipāśāśca muktāḥ sūryeṇa raśmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Oṃ, released are the bonds, freed are the fetters, released are the rays by the sun,

children.text: muktaḥ sarvabhayādgarbha ehyehi mā cira svāhā // JPanc_3.83 //
children.translated_text: freed from all fears, O child in the womb, come forth, come forth, do not delay, <s>svāhā</s>! // JPanc_3.83 //

children.text: ebhirjalaṃ cyāvanamantrarājairjaptvā pradeyaṃ kila garbhavatyai /
children.translated_text: Having recited these supreme mantras over water, it should be given to the pregnant woman;

children.text: sadyaḥ prasūte navamūḍhagarbhā yogo 'yamātreyamunipradiṣṭaḥ // JPanc_3.84 //
children.translated_text: she who has a difficult or obstructed delivery will give birth immediately — this practice was prescribed by the sage <s>Ātreya</s>. // JPanc_3.84 //

children.text:
ebhirmantraiḥ saptavāramabhimantritaṃ jalaṃ garbhavatyai pātuṃ dātavyam /
"oṃ manmatha manmatha manmathavāhini ! lambodaraṃ muñca muñca laghu svāhā" iti mantraḥ / anena mantreṇa saptavāramabhimantritaṃ jalaṃ garbhavatyai pātuṃ dātavyam / sukhāt prasavo bhavati //
children.translated_text: Water consecrated seven times with these mantras should be given to the pregnant woman to drink. "Oṃ <s>Manmatha</s>, <s>Manmatha</s>, O bearer of <s>Manmatha</s>! Release the large-bellied one, release quickly, <s>svāhā</s>" — this is the mantra. Water consecrated seven times with this mantra should be given to the pregnant woman to drink. An easy delivery will result.

children.text: atha vandhyākaraṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on inducing barrenness.

children.text: palāśakṣīridrumayoḥ phalāni puṣpāṇyatho śālmalipādapasya /
children.translated_text: The fruits of the <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma) and the milk-tree (<s>kṣīridruma</s>), and the flowers of the <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) tree —

children.text: madyena māsārdhadinaṃ nipīya vandhyā bhavenniścitameva nārī // JPanc_3.85 //
children.translated_text: if a woman drinks these with liquor for half a month, she will certainly become barren. // JPanc_3.85 //

children.text: phalaṃ kadambasya ca mākṣikaṃ hi tuṣodakena tridinaṃ nipīya /
children.translated_text: The fruit of <s>kadamba</s> (Neolamarckia cadamba) together with honey, drunk for three days with rice-water,

children.text: snānāvasāne niyamena cāpi vandhyāmavaśyaṃ kurute haṭhena // JPanc_3.86 //
children.translated_text: after bathing, with strict observance — this forcibly and certainly makes a woman barren. // JPanc_3.86 //

children.text: karṣadvayaṃ rākṣasavṛkṣabījaṃ saptāhamātraṃ sitaśālivārā /
children.translated_text: Two <s>karṣas</s> of the seeds of the <s>rākṣasa</s> tree (castor plant), taken with white rice gruel for seven days,

children.text: ṛtau nipītaṃ mṛgaśāvakākṣyā vandhyātvametanniyataṃ karoti // JPanc_3.87 //
children.translated_text: drunk during the menstrual period by the doe-eyed woman — this assuredly induces barrenness. // JPanc_3.87 //

children.text: atha keśasaṃskārasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on hair care.

children.text: tilaprasūnaṃ saha gokṣureṇa sasāraghaṃ gavyaghṛtena piṣṭam /
children.translated_text: The flower of <s>tila</s> (sesame) together with <s>gokṣura</s> (Tribulus terrestris), mixed with <s>sāraghā</s> and cow's ghee, ground into a paste —

children.text: saptāhamātreṇa śiraḥpralepādbhavanti dīrghāḥ pracurāśca keśāḥ // JPanc_3.88 //
children.translated_text: by applying this to the head for just seven days, the hair becomes long and abundant. // JPanc_3.88 //

children.text: karṣārdhamātraṃ prasavaṃ phalena nimbasya tailaṃ niyamena pītam /
children.translated_text: Half a <s>karṣa</s> measure of the fruit of the <s>nimba</s> (neem) tree, its oil drunk regularly,

children.text: krameṇa kundendutuṣāragauraṃ śiroruhaṃ mecakatāmupaiti // JPanc_3.89 //
children.translated_text: gradually the hair, though dark as collyrium, attains the whiteness of <s>kunda</s> flowers, the moon, and snow. // JPanc_3.89 //

children.text: atha indraluptasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on <s>indralupta</s> (alopecia).

children.text: guñjāphalaiḥ kṣaudrayutairvilipya keśapradeśe sakalendraluptam /
children.translated_text: By anointing the hair region affected with complete <s>indralupta</s> with <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus precatorius) seeds mixed with honey,

children.text: anena yogena sadaiva keśā rohanti kṛṣṇāḥ kuṭilā viśālāḥ // JPanc_3.90 //
children.translated_text: through this remedy, the hair always grows back — dark, curly, and thick. // JPanc_3.90 //

children.text: iti śrīkaviśekharajyotirīśaviracite pañcasāyake tṛtīyaḥ sāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>sāyaka</s> (arrow) in the <s>Pañcasāyaka</s> composed by <s>Jyotirīśa Kaviśekhara</s>.

children.text: atha caturthaḥ sāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the fourth <s>sāyaka</s> (arrow).

children.text: atha kanyālakṣaṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on the characteristics of an ideal bride.

children.text: prakhyāte mahati prabhūtavibhave cāritraśīlānvite vidyādhairyavivekaśauryavibhavaślāghye kulīne kule /
children.translated_text: In a family that is renowned, great, abundantly wealthy, endowed with virtuous conduct, praiseworthy for its learning, fortitude, discernment, valor, and prosperity, and of noble lineage —

children.text: kanyā bhrātṛyutā suśīlavinayā rūpojjvalā dakṣiṇā traivargāśritaśuddhavaṃśanilayā sadbhirvivāhyā naraiḥ // JPanc_4.1 //
children.translated_text: a maiden who has brothers, possesses good character and modesty, is radiant in beauty, gracious, dwelling in a pure lineage devoted to the three aims of life — such a one should be married by worthy men. // JPanc_4.1 //

children.text: ambhojāsyā bahalanayanā bhūrikeśapracārā tulyā snigdhā susamadaśanā padmarāgādharauṣṭhī /
children.translated_text: With a lotus-like face, large eyes, abundant flowing hair, of even complexion, affectionate, with well-matched teeth, lips like <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby),

children.text: ramyaśrotrā madhuravacanā kambukaṇṭhī śubhāṅgī madhye kṣīṇā sulalitakarā dakṣiṇāvartanābhiḥ // JPanc_4.2 //
children.translated_text: with beautiful ears, sweet-spoken, with a conch-like neck, auspicious-limbed, slender at the waist, with graceful hands, and a clockwise-spiraling navel, // JPanc_4.2 //

children.text: pīnaśroṇī kanakakadalīstambhajaṅghābhirāmā raktāśokaprasavacaraṇā snigdhaśākhāṅgulīkā /
children.translated_text: with full hips, thighs lovely as the stems of golden plantains, feet like fresh <s>aśoka</s> blossoms, smooth branch-like fingers —

children.text: itthaṃ yuktā sulalitatanurlakṣaṇairuttamairyā kanyā sadbhiścaṭulacaritā sā vivāhyā guṇajñaiḥ // JPanc_4.3 //
children.translated_text: a maiden endowed thus with a graceful form and these excellent characteristics, of lively disposition — she should be married by the wise who appreciate virtues. // JPanc_4.3 //

children.text: atha kanyādūṣaṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on defects of brides.

children.text: kharvā piṅgalakuntalā kṛśatanurdīrghā 'tiromākulā kṛṣṇā saukaralocanā pṛthugalā kṛṣṇādharā danturā /
children.translated_text: A woman who is dwarfish, tawny-haired, thin-bodied, excessively tall, covered with body hair, dark-complexioned, pig-eyed, thick-necked, dark-lipped, buck-toothed,

children.text: rukṣāṅgī vikaṭastanī ca sabalā babhrūravīrātmajā vācālā bahubhojanā ca gadinī prauḍhā ca duḥkhānvitā // JPanc_4.4 //
children.translated_text: rough-skinned, with misshapen breasts, spotted, brown-complexioned, born of a cowardly family, garrulous, gluttonous, sickly, aged, and full of sorrow — // JPanc_4.4 //

children.text: puṣpakṣmādharavṛkṣadeśataṭinīnakṣatrasañjñā ca yā hāsye kūpayugaṃ kapolayugale yasyā bhavet satvaram /
children.translated_text: she whose eyebrows, lips, body hair, and moles bear names of trees, rivers, or <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar asterisms), who has dimples on both cheeks that appear when she laughs,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhādhikaparvaṇī caraṇayoryasyāśca jātā 'ṅguliḥ pādasyāpi kanīnikā na patati kṣmāyāṃ tadanyaiva vā // JPanc_4.5 //
children.translated_text: whose toes have extra joints beyond the thumb, or whose little toe of the foot does not touch the ground, or any other such sign — // JPanc_4.5 //

children.text: ajñātānvayajā svabhāvapiśunā lambādharā cañcalā kuṣṭhiścitrikulodbhavā ca vitatā yasyāḥ kaṭirnāsikā /
children.translated_text: born of unknown lineage, treacherous by nature, with a drooping lower lip, fickle, afflicted with skin disease, born of a mottled family, with a broad flat nose,

children.text: nindyā pallavajihvikā drutagatirnyūnādhikāṅgī punas tyājyā kāmakalākalāpakuśalaiḥ kanyā vivāhe sadā // JPanc_4.6 //
children.translated_text: blamed for having a tongue like a sprout, walking hastily, with limbs deficient or excessive — such a maiden should always be rejected in marriage by those skilled in the arts of love. // JPanc_4.6 //

children.text: atha varalakṣaṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on the characteristics of an ideal groom.

children.text: prakhyāto 'malavaṃśajo navavayāḥ śūrassuśīlaśca yaḥ svācāraḥ sthirasauhṛdo guṇanidhirnānākuṭumbī balī /
children.translated_text: He who is renowned, of pure lineage, youthful, valorous, of good character, righteous in conduct, steadfast in friendship, a treasury of virtues, maintaining many dependents, strong,

children.text: arthī bhogarato viśiṣṭavacano dākṣiṇyadhairyāśrayo jāmātā jagatītale kavivarairevaṃvidho varṇitaḥ // JPanc_4.7 //
children.translated_text: prosperous, devoted to pleasures, distinguished in speech, a refuge of generosity and fortitude — such a son-in-law has been described by the best of poets as ideal on this earth. // JPanc_4.7 //

children.text: atha varadūṣaṇasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on defects of grooms.

children.text: pāpiṣṭho vyasanī ṛṇairupahato dyūtapriyo bhikṣuko rogī puṃstvavivarjitaścalamatirvaideśikaḥ kātaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Sinful, addicted to vices, burdened with debts, fond of gambling, a beggar, sickly, devoid of manhood, fickle-minded, a foreigner, cowardly,

children.text: mūrkho duṣṭakulodbhavaśca kṛpaṇo vṛddho 'tidīnaḥ khalaḥ kartavyo na varaḥ kadā 'pi puruṣairevaṃvidho bhūtale // JPanc_4.8 //
children.translated_text: foolish, born of a wicked family, miserly, old, utterly wretched, and malicious — such a man should never be accepted as a groom by people on this earth. // JPanc_4.8 //

children.text: atha vivāhabhedasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on the types of marriage.

children.text: cāturvarṇyasamāhitā munivarairaṣṭau vivāhāḥ striyo brāhmo daivatakastato nigaditau gāndharvapaiśācakau /
children.translated_text: Established for the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), eight types of marriage for women have been declared by the great sages: <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, then <s>Gāndharva</s> and <s>Paiśāca</s>,

children.text: ārṣo rākṣasakastathā ' 'sura iti khyāto 'paraścāṣṭamaḥ prājāpatyasamābhidhaḥ pṛthagamī proktā mayā nāmataḥ // JPanc_4.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and then <s>Āsura</s> — thus is the seventh known, and the eighth is called <s>Prājāpatya</s>; I have stated them individually by name. // JPanc_4.9 //

children.text: ārṣo daivatakaḥ prajāpatibhavo brāhmo dvijānāṃ mato gāndharvaḥ saha rākṣasena kathitaḥ kṣātrasya tajjñairasau /
children.translated_text: <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and <s>Brāhma</s> are prescribed for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; <s>Gāndharva</s> together with <s>Rākṣasa</s> is declared by the knowledgeable for <s>Kṣatriyas</s>;

children.text: ekaścāsurasañjñako nigadito vaiśyasya śūdrasya ca saṅkṣepādupavarṇitaṃ kramavaśātpaurāṇikaṃ lakṣaṇam // JPanc_4.10 //
children.translated_text: and the one called <s>Āsura</s> is stated for <s>Vaiśyas</s> and <s>Śūdras</s> — thus is briefly described in sequence the characteristic as found in the <s>Purāṇas</s>. // JPanc_4.10 //

children.text: vidyāvān guṇapūjitaḥ sucaritaḥ sadvaṃśajāto muniḥ saumyo mānarataḥ suśīlavinayo gehāgataḥ prārthakaḥ /
children.translated_text: A sage who is learned, honored for his virtues, of good conduct, born of a noble lineage, gentle, devoted to honor, of good character and modesty, who comes to the house as a suitor —

children.text: kanyāyā gṛhanāyakaḥ sapulakastasmai dadātyādarād ārṣo goyugadakṣiṇo nigaditastajjñairvivāho varaḥ // JPanc_4.11 //
children.translated_text: the head of the household, thrilled with joy, gives his daughter to him with respect; this, with a pair of cows as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (gift), is declared by the knowledgeable to be the excellent <s>Ārṣa</s> marriage. // JPanc_4.11 //

children.text: ṛtvigbhiḥ parimaṇḍite bahuvidhe yajñotsave cottame nānāvarṇasuvarṇavastrakusumairābhūṣitāṅgī śubhā /
children.translated_text: At a grand sacrificial festival (<s>yajña</s>) elaborately adorned by <s>ṛtvijs</s> (officiating priests), of many kinds and of the highest order, the bride adorned with garments and flowers of various colors and gold, auspicious —

children.text: kanyā dakṣiṇayā dvijāya vidhinā yaddīyate cādarād daivaḥ so 'yamudīritaḥ kavivarairitthaṃ vivāho varaḥ // JPanc_4.12 //
children.translated_text: when the maiden is given with propriety and respect to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> along with <s>dakṣiṇā</s> — this has been proclaimed by the best poets as the excellent <s>Daiva</s> marriage. // JPanc_4.12 //

children.text: kanyā bāndhvasannidhau sulalitā viprottamāyādarād uktvā- tubhyamiyaṃ mayā svatanayā datteti harṣānvitau /
children.translated_text: When the graceful maiden, in the presence of relatives, is given respectfully to an excellent <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with the words: 'This daughter of mine is given to you,' and both are filled with joy,

children.text: dharmaṃ sañcaratāṃ yathāsukhamubhau dāmpatyayogātsadā prājāpatyakaragraha kavivaraireṣaḥ pramāṇīkṛtaḥ // JPanc_4.13 //
children.translated_text: 'May you both pursue <s>dharma</s> happily together always through the union of marriage' — this <s>Prājāpatya</s> hand-clasping marriage has been validated by the best poets. // JPanc_4.13 //

children.text: āhūyārcanapūrvakaṃ dvijavarāyācchādya vāsovarair vidyāśīlavivekavaṃśavinayācārānvitāya svayam /
children.translated_text: Having invited and worshipped an excellent <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, covering him with fine garments, one who is endowed with learning, virtue, discernment, lineage, modesty, and good conduct —

children.text: kanyā prītimate varāya vidhinā yaddīyate sādaraṃ brāhmo 'sau munipuṅgavairnigaditaḥ śreṣṭho vivāho 'paraḥ // JPanc_4.14 //
children.translated_text: when the maiden is given with propriety and affection to such a worthy and beloved groom — this is the <s>Brāhma</s> marriage, declared by the foremost sages as another excellent form. // JPanc_4.14 //

children.text: kanyā yauvanaśālinī patimamuṃ yā svīkaroti svayaṃ gāndharvaḥ sa hi kathyate bhujabalādākṛṣyate yatpunaḥ /
children.translated_text: When a maiden in the bloom of youth chooses her husband herself, that is called <s>Gāndharva</s>; when she is seized by force,

children.text: jñeyo rākṣasa eṣa paṇḍitavaraiścauryādvivāho 'paraḥ paiśācaḥ kaviśekhareṇa kathitastyājyaḥ sadā yatnataḥ // JPanc_4.15 //
children.translated_text: that is to be known as <s>Rākṣasa</s> by the learned; another marriage by stealth is <s>Paiśāca</s>, declared by <s>Kaviśekhara</s> as always to be carefully avoided. // JPanc_4.15 //

children.text: ādāya prathamaṃ varādbahutaraṃ śulkaṃ yathākāṅkṣayā vastrālaṅkṛtivaibhavena tanayāsantoṣamutpādya ca /
children.translated_text: First receiving from the groom an abundant bride-price (<s>śulka</s>) as desired, and gratifying the daughter with garments, ornaments, and wealth,

children.text: paścādduṣkulasambhavāya malinaṃ kanyāpradānaṃ vṛthā prakhyāto 'dhamavaṃśajāpariṇayastajjñairasāvāsuraḥ // JPanc_4.16 //

children.text: atha paradāratyāgasamuddeśaḥ /

children.text: atha dūtīsamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now begins the section on the messenger (<s>dūtī</s>).

children.text: cakṣuḥprītirudīritā prathamataścittabhramaḥ syāttataḥ saṅkalpastadanantaraṃ nigadito nidrāvināśastathā /

children.translated_text: then dispassion toward sense objects, then emaciation, then the abandonment of shame, then madness, and finally death — these ten (or nine) are declared to be the stages of <s>Kāma's</s> (Love's) influence. // JPanc_4.19 //

children.translated_text: Therefore, for the prevention of that, desirous men should resort to another's woman — so say <s>Kāśyapa</s> Muni, <s>Kṣemendra</s>, and <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: tārāpīḍasuto vināśamagamatkādambarīkāṅkṣayā vyāmuktaḥ kila puṇḍarīkamunirapyuccairmahāśvetayā /

children.text: dāsī vāravadhūrnaṭī ca vidhavā bālā ca dhātrī tathā kanyā pravrajitā ca bhikṣuvanitā sambandhinī śilpinī /
children.translated_text: A maidservant, a courtesan, a dancer, a widow, a young girl, a wet-nurse, likewise a maiden, a female renunciant, a mendicant's wife, a kinswoman, an artisan-woman,

children.text: atha suratayogyasthānasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the section on places suitable for lovemaking.

children.text: sphūrjjaddīpaśikhojjvale sulalite ramyonnate vistare dhūpodgāramanohare kusumasragdāmopaśobhānvite /

children.text: athābhilāṣasamuddeśaḥ /

children.text: atha puruṣāyitasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on the <s>puruṣāyita</s> (woman-on-top) position.

children.text: adhomukhī kāntahṛdi prasuptā dorbhyāṃ samāliṅgya yadi prayāti /
children.translated_text: If [the woman], face-down upon her lover's chest, embracing [him] with both arms, proceeds [with the act],

children.text: gā(prau)ḍhāṅganāvallabha eṣa tajjñaiḥ bandhaḥ pradiṣṭo viparītarūpaḥ // JPanc_5.23 //
children.translated_text: This position, beloved of mature women, is declared by the knowledgeable as <s>viparīta</s> (reversed).

children.text: dhūrta ! tvamevaṃ vijito 'syakasmādyuddhe mayā pañcaśarasya nārī /
children.translated_text: "O rogue! You have been defeated by me thus, unexpectedly, in the battle of the five-arrowed one (love-god)!" — a woman,

children.text: ityādikaṃ bhūrividhaṃ raṭantī prāyaḥ sukhaṃ vindati keliraṅge // JPanc_5.24 //
children.translated_text: Proclaiming such and various other things, generally finds pleasure in the arena of love-play.

children.text: viparītaratāvayogyāṃ striyaṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: He shows the woman unfit for the reversed position:

children.text: navaprasūtā ṛtuyogayuktā garbhālasā sthūlatanurnatāṅgī /
children.translated_text: A newly delivered mother, one in her fertile period, one sluggish with pregnancy, one with a stout body, one with a bent body,

children.text: kṣīṇā navoḍhā jvaritā ca nārī varjyā ratijñairviparītabandhe // JPanc_5.25 //
children.translated_text: An emaciated woman, a newly married woman, and a feverish woman—these should be avoided by those who know the art of love in the reversed position.

children.text: atha santāḍitasamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, section on striking (<s>santāḍita</s>).

children.text: vāmasvabhāvānmadanasya rāgo hastaprahārātsamupaiti vṛddhim /
children.translated_text: Since <s>Madana</s> (the love god) is of contrary nature, passion increases from hand-strikes;

children.text: tasmādyathāsthānamasau vidheyo varāṅganāyāḥ suratāvasāne // JPanc_5.26 //
children.translated_text: therefore, they should be applied to the appropriate places on the body of the excellent woman at the conclusion of love-making. // JPanc_5.26 //

children.text: yadyaṅganā kāntahṛdi prahāraṃ muṣṭyā bhajantī suratopacāraiḥ /
children.translated_text: When a woman, reciprocating the love-play, strikes the heart of her beloved with a fist,

children.text: santāḍitaṃ nāma vadanti tajjñā vistīrṇahastena tadā patākam // JPanc_5.27 //
children.translated_text: the experts call it <s>santāḍita</s> (striking); when with the spread palm, it is called <s>patāka</s> (the banner). // JPanc_5.27 //

children.text: sāṅguṣṭhamadhyāṅgulasamprahārāt sañjāyate kuṇḍalanāmadheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: From a blow with the thumb and middle finger arises what is named <s>kuṇḍala</s> (the ring);

children.text: yaḥ kevalāṅguṣṭhabhavo 'bhighātaḥ proktaḥ kavīndraiḥ sa tu bindumālaḥ // JPanc_5.28 //
children.translated_text: the blow produced by the thumb alone — the great poets call it <s>bindumāla</s> (the row of drops). // JPanc_5.28 //

children.text: dravati yadi na nārī prauḍharāgārtiyuktā mṛdunidhuvanayoge dantasandhau salīlam /
children.translated_text: When the woman, overcome with intense passion, does not melt in the gentle love-play, [she should] playfully [bite] at the junction of the teeth;

children.text: pibati daśanavāsaḥ kiñcidunmucya bhūyaḥ kathitamiha rasajñaiḥ sītkṛtaṃ rāgakāri // JPanc_5.29 //
children.translated_text: releasing the lip-hold slightly, she drinks again — the connoisseurs of pleasure describe this as <s>sītkṛta</s> (the hiss), which arouses passion. // JPanc_5.29 //

children.text: pikaśikhikalahaṃsaprāyapakṣivṛjānāṃ dhvanitamanukarotītyaṅganā manmathārtā /
children.translated_text: The woman tormented by love imitates the calls of flocks of birds such as the cuckoo, peacock, and <s>kalahaṃsa</s> (swan);

children.text: mukhadaśanavivartāttatkavīndrā vadanti stanitamiti samāsāccitrasambhogakāle // JPanc_5.30 //
children.translated_text: the great poets say these sounds from the twisting of the mouth and teeth are called <s>stanita</s> (thunder), in brief, during the varied love-play. // JPanc_5.30 //

children.text: evaṃvidhakaraṇasya phalaṃ nirūpayati /
children.translated_text: He describes the fruit of such practices:

children.text: ityādiyogaiḥ pṛthukāmabhāvaṃ sampādya nārīpuruṣau cireṇa /
children.translated_text: By these and other methods, having cultivated the expansive state of desire over a long time, the woman and the man,

children.text: jātānurāgau rahasi prakāmaṃ saukhyaṃ samāsvādayato mahīyaḥ // JPanc_5.31 //
children.translated_text: having developed mutual love, savor in private to their heart's content the supreme pleasure. // JPanc_5.31 //

children.text: aṣṭānāyikāsamuddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The section on the eight <s>nāyikās</s> (heroines).

children.text: yasyāḥ patirmilati kelikathānuraktaḥ pārśvaṃ na muñcati manobhavavegayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: She whose husband meets her, devoted to amorous talk, does not leave her side, impelled by the force of love —

children.text: syātsundarī sakalasaukhyakalānidhānā svādhīnapūrvapatiketi vadanti tajjñāḥ // JPanc_5.32 //
children.translated_text: that beautiful woman, the treasury of all arts of pleasure, the experts call <s>svādhīnapatikā</s> (she whose lord is under her control). // JPanc_5.32 //

children.text: puṣpāṅgarāgarucirā taruṇī priyasya tiṣṭhatyanāgamanahetuvicāralolā /
children.translated_text: Adorned with flowers and cosmetics, the young woman stands pondering the reasons for her beloved's non-arrival;

children.text: eṣā 'balā na hi ciraṃ paridevanīyā sotkaṇṭhiteti kathitā kavibhiḥ purāṇaiḥ // JPanc_5.33 //
children.translated_text: this woman should not be mourned for long — the ancient poets have called her <s>utkaṇṭhitā</s> (the yearning one). // JPanc_5.33 //

children.text: srakcandanāmbaravibhūṣaṇabhūṣitāṅgī yā vallabhāgamanamārgavirūḍhadṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: She whose limbs are adorned with garlands, sandalwood, garments, and ornaments, whose gaze is fixed upon the path of her beloved's arrival,

children.text: talpaṃ gatā ruciravāsagṛhe 'vaśete sā kīrtitā jagati vāsakasajjiteti // JPanc_5.34 //
children.translated_text: who has gone to the bed and waits in the beautiful pleasure-chamber — she is celebrated in the world as <s>vāsakasajjitā</s> (dressed for the tryst). // JPanc_5.34 //

children.text: krodhātprayāti caraṇe patito 'pi kāntaḥ prāyaḥ pracaṇḍavacanāccaraṇairnirastaḥ /
children.translated_text: Out of anger she departs even though the lover has fallen at her feet; [he is] mostly rebuffed by harsh words and kicks;

children.text: paścāttadīyavirahakṣaradānatāṅgī sā kīrtiteha kalahāntaritā kavīndraiḥ // JPanc_5.35 //
children.translated_text: afterward, her body oozing with grief from separation from him — she is celebrated here by the great poets as <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (the one estranged by quarrel). // JPanc_5.35 //

children.text: saṅketakaṃ priyatamaḥ svayameva dattvā naivāgataḥ samucite samaye ca yasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Her beloved himself having given the rendezvous, yet did not come at the appointed time;

children.text: hṛṣṭā vaco 'mṛtarasaiḥ sakalāṅgayaṣṭiḥ sā varṇitā kavivarairiha vipralabdhā // JPanc_5.36 //
children.translated_text: her whole body-stalk [trembles], her joyful words [turn to] nectar-juice [tears] — she is described by the best poets as <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one). // JPanc_5.36 //

children.text: prātarvinidravadanasmarabhāracauro nidrālaso 'lasagatirnakhavikṣatāṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: With face bearing the traces of morning sleep, beauty stolen by the weight of love, languid with drowsiness, slow of gait, body scratched by nails —

children.text: yasyāḥ prayātyabhimukhaṃ muhuśo yuvatyāḥ sā khaṇḍiteti kathitā kavibhiḥ purāṇaiḥ // JPanc_5.37 //
children.translated_text: he who approaches the young woman repeatedly [in this state] — she is called by the ancient poets <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the woman with a faithless lover). // JPanc_5.37 //

children.text: ārambhabhagnacaritā vikalā ca nārī yā nirmitā hi madanena madena yāti /
children.translated_text: The woman of broken resolve, distressed, fashioned by <s>Madana</s> (the love god), goes forth intoxicated with passion,

children.text: guptābhisārarasikā paraveśma gantuṃ sā kīrtitā kavivarairabhisāriketi // JPanc_5.38 //
children.translated_text: eager for the pleasure of a secret assignation, to go to another's house — she is celebrated by the best poets as <s>abhisārikā</s> (the one who goes to a tryst). // JPanc_5.38 //

children.text: deśāntaraṃ prativasadramaṇaśca yasyā dattvā 'vadhiṃ cirataraṃ gurukāryayogāt /
children.translated_text: She whose lover dwells in a distant land, having set a date and been gone for a very long time due to weighty duties,

children.text: durvāraduḥkhadahanaiḥ paridevitāṅgī sā proṣitapriyatamā kathitā munīndraiḥ // JPanc_5.39 //
children.translated_text: whose body laments with the irresistible fire of grief — she is called by the great sages <s>proṣitapriyatamā</s> (she whose beloved is abroad). // JPanc_5.39 //

children.text: granthopasaṃhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Conclusion of the work.

children.text: yāvaccandrakalākirīṭahṛdaye śailādhirājātmajā yāvadvakṣasi mādhavasya kamalā sānandamādīvyati /
children.translated_text: As long as the daughter of the king of mountains (<s>Pārvatī</s>) joyfully sports in the heart of the Moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>), as long as <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) blissfully delights upon the chest of <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),

children.text: yāvatkāmakalāvivartacaṭulaṃ kṣoṇītalaṃ rājate tāvacchrīkaviśekharasya kṛtinaḥ kāvyaṃ mude dīvyatām // JPanc_5.40 //
children.translated_text: as long as the earth shines, restless with the play of the arts of <s>Kāma</s> — so long may this poem of the meritorious <s>Śrī Kaviśekhara</s> sport for [the world's] delight! // JPanc_5.40 //

children.text: iti kaviśekharaśrījyotīśvarācāryaviracite pañcasāyake pañcamaḥ sāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth arrow in the <s>Pañcasāyaka</s>, composed by the teacher <s>Śrī Jyotīśvara Kaviśekhara</s>.

children.text: samāptaścāyaṃ granthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And this work is complete. //
